correctness.rationale: The binary 2-binomial signature is proved from all six scattered-subsequence counts. Every position decomposes uniquely as 128j+r, and every length-72 window is captured by one of 4×128 explicit morphism templates. Two different implementations (integer first moments and direct scattered-subsequence enumeration) agree on every candidate root in every template. The complete table proves the exact least-root levels and sharp maximum; its rational pair-frequency weighting, derived from the primitive substitution, gives all densities. Every boundary and quantifier is covered.

evidence: Lejeune–Leroy–Rigo (2020), introduction and binomial-complexity theorem, counts classes of individual factors at each length; it does not characterize pairs of consecutive factors at a common start.
Rigo–Salimov (2013), Thue–Morse complexity and avoidance section, proves bounded binomial complexity and discusses square avoidance, not the local minimum.
Rao–Rigo–Salimov (2015) establishes avoidability of binomial squares over a ternary alphabet; the constructed sequence is not the binary Thue–Morse fixed point.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Global boundedness or exact counts of equivalence classes among length-m factors do not imply that two adjacent factors match at a position, nor determine their smallest common length. General existence of some matching roots fails to determine the worst local minimum or its exact density.

originality.rationale: A complete all-start least-root distribution with sharp maximum 36 and exact nine-level density spectrum is neither a mere existence statement nor a factor-equivalence-class count. Inspection of the 2013, 2015 and 2020 primary papers revealed no statement covering these conditional local minima or position densities. Public mathematical record searches and the required current research-record comparisons returned no equivalent claim. Remaining historical-priority uncertainty is recorded, not hidden.
residual_risks: An unindexed independent enumeration of local 2-binomial-square radii may predate this work.
The complete review did not establish mathematical priority against all unpublished papers or software outputs.
The finite exhaustive table must be independently replayed in any external validation.

value.rationale: Binomial-square existence and 2-binomial equivalence are established topics. The least square root starting at each index is a natural local-repetition invariant. This proof supplies a uniform sharp bound for all infinitely many starting positions, a complete nine-value minimum-root spectrum, a precise characterization of worst positions, and their exact density (1/96). These statements are not a routine reformulation of global factor-complexity counts or existence of roots somewhere.
